newsitem.title: USA: AT&T moves to provide California local service.
newsitem.headline: AT&T moves to provide California local service.

text.p: AT&T Corp said it filed a tariff Wednesday to provide local telephone service to California residential customers, with a controlled introduction of service to begin in Sacramento.

AT&T said it filed the public notice with the California Public Utilities Commission, the state utilities regulator, advising it plans to launch local service in the northern California area where Pacific Telesis Group's Pacific Bell unit has until now dominated the local phone market.
AT&T will begin offering local telephone service in Sacramento next Monday, company spokeswoman Alice Nagle said.

"Once we're sure that our operations and the systems interfaces with Pacific Bell are up to the world-class standards that customers have come to expect from AT&T, we plan to offer local service to consumers throughout California," AT&T Pacific States President Michael Antieri said.

AT&T said it will give California customers a single bill for long-distance and local service with simplified pricing. The company also offers Sacramento consumers wireless calling, on-line services and access to home entertainment.
A new competitive framework approved by regulators allows long-distance telephone companies to compete in providing local services in California with the former local phone service monopolies.

AT&T is initially serving customers by reselling local phone service from Pacific Bell. AT&T said any company's ability to successfully compete with the long-standing local telephone monopolies still rests largely with state and federal regulators.

"The California Public Utilities Commission has been at the forefront of the effort to bring the benefits of competition to consumers," Antieri said. "But a truly open and competitive market still hinges on whether the commission follows the letter and spirit of the Federal Telecommunications Act in developing the rules and prices for opening up the local phone market," he added.
